conviction_note: Peers that printed after Southwest's July guide (DAL 10-09, UAL 10-20) show both halves of this print: unit revenue +15-17% with Q4 revenue accelerating past +20%, and jet fuel running above LUV's unhedged $3.70-3.75 Q3 assumption with a Q4 curve near $4.80/gal that should force a cut to the $3.25-4.25 FY guide. UAL rose about 5% today on exactly that mix, LUV has fallen on 5 of its last 7 prints, and the skew leans slightly to upside, so the near-flat lean (p_up 47) is the honest read on 7 points of absolute move. The findings sum (-0.2) and the scaled number (-0.42) agree in sign and size. The web-search budget was used up at the start of this hunt, so every source here was fetched directly (EDGAR, Yahoo chart, TSA) and sell-side consensus could not be reached.
bar: Company guide only: Q3 2026 adjusted EPS $0.50-0.75, RASM +17.5% to +19.5% yoy, ASMs -1% to flat, CASM-x +3.5% to +4.0%, fuel $3.70-3.75/gal on the July 17 curve; FY2026 adjusted EPS $3.25-4.25 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/92380/000009238026000074/er-6302026xerdoc.htm, 2026-07-22). The sell-side consensus is UNSOURCED: web search was unavailable this run, and no two estimate sources could be read. Every finding is capped small for that reason. print_vs_bar_pct refers to revenue against the guided RASM midpoint (+18.5% on roughly flat capacity).
positioning_check: Short interest is about 32.9M shares, roughly 6.7% of float and 5.7 days to cover, from an August 2026 Equibles snapshot carried in the sweep row (https://equibles.com/stocks/LUV). That is not crowded and is stale by about two months. Skew is -2.6 vol points (25d put IV minus 25d call IV), so the market pays slightly more for upside; put/call OI 0.58 (baseline, 2026-10-21). The event-implied move is 6.47%, but the ATM spread is 79% of mid, so it is only indicative. Holders at 9/30: PRIMECAP 10.02% (49.0M shares, 13G/A filed 2026-10-05) and Franklin Templeton 10.2% including Putnam 7.6% (13G/A filed 2026-10-07). Run-up: +2.47% over 5 days, -1.78% over 20 days, -26.4% from the 52-week high. The sector sold off Oct 12-19 (LUV 41.66 to 38.80) and bounced Oct 20-21 (LUV ~40.4 at 12:22 ET).

findings.finding: Q3 jet fuel ran above Southwest's assumption, and Southwest is unhedged. United's Q3 average was $3.90/gal (+60% yoy). Delta's GAAP fuel was $3.80/gal, and Delta said it absorbed more than $500M of fuel above its early-July guidance. Southwest guided Q3 at $3.70-3.75/gal on the July 17 curve and burned 564M gallons in Q2. An overage of about $0.15-0.20/gal is $85-113M pre-tax, or about $0.13-0.17 of adjusted EPS on 493M diluted shares. That would put Q3 adjusted EPS near or below the low end of the $0.50-0.75 guide unless RASM beats the +17.5-19.5% guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q2 2026 Southwest's fuel came in below assumption ($3.92 vs $4.10-4.15) and the FY guide was still cut; the stock fell 6.19% on 2026-07-22. LUV has fallen on 5 of its last 7 prints (baseline).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. Fuel is public, and analysts mark EPS to the curve, which is part of why LUV fell from 41.66 (10-09) to 38.80 (10-19). But the company has not updated its Q3 fuel assumption since July 22: there has been no 7.01 investor-update 8-K since then (EDGAR list). If the market had fully priced the overage, the 10-20/10-21 sector bounce would have left LUV lagging, and it did not (+4.2% off the low).
findings.independence: Delta's Q3 release is a separate document: GAAP fuel $3.80/gal, more than $500M above early-July guidance (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/27904/000002790426000035/deltaairlinesannouncessept.htm). Southwest's own unhedged status and gallons come from https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/92380/000009238026000074/er-6302026xerdoc.htm.

findings.finding: United's investor update puts Q4 2026 fuel at about $4.80/gal on the October 16 Gulf Coast curve. It also states that consensus assumes about $4.35/gal, $0.45 below its own assumption. Against a Q3 run rate near $3.90, an unhedged Southwest burning about 565M gallons faces roughly $500M of extra pre-tax Q4 fuel, about $0.75-0.80 per share after tax. The FY2026 adjusted EPS guide of $3.25-4.25 was set on the July 17 curve, so a cut or a low Q4 guide is likely, and the street may be marked to a stale fuel assumption as United says its own consensus is.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance has moved LUV most. FY guide cut on 2026-07-22: -6.19%. Guide on 2026-01-28: +18.7%. United's own fuel-heavy, below-consensus Q4 EPS guide ($0.50-1.50) was bought: UAL rose from 97.77 to 102.90 by 12:22 ET on 2026-10-21.
findings.why_not_priced: United says in its own document that consensus fuel lags the curve by $0.45/gal. If LUV's estimates were already marked to $4.80, its FY range would already be treated as broken, and the stock would not have bounced with the sector on 10-20/10-21. The reaction is the open question, not the fact: UAL was bought on the same mix.
findings.independence: Delta's October 2 curve implied about $4.25/gal all-in after a $0.40 refinery benefit, so about $4.65 before it, which points the same way (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/27904/000002790426000035/deltaairlinesannouncessept.htm). This shares the UAL filing with the peer-revenue finding below, but rests on a different line of it.

findings.finding: Peers that reported after Southwest's July guide show domestic and main-cabin unit revenue up about 15-17% and Q4 revenue accelerating. Delta: domestic unit revenue +16%, main cabin unit revenue +17% on fewer seats, Q4 revenue guided about +20%, 'revenue momentum is continuing'. United: domestic PRASM +14.5%, economy unit revenue +17%, Q4 revenue growth to accelerate past +20%. That supports Southwest landing inside or above its +17.5-19.5% Q3 RASM guide (it beat its Q2 RASM guide with +20.1%) and guiding Q4 RASM strongly enough to offset part of the fuel hit.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Southwest's last print with an above-guide RASM (Q2 2026, +20.1%) still fell 6.19% because the EPS guide was cut. Its revenue-led initiatives guide in January 2026 rose 18.7%.
findings.why_not_priced: Peer revenue is public. What is not public is Southwest's Q4 RASM number, its first statement since July 22. Southwest's guided Q3 RASM is above peers' realised TRASM, so peers confirming the fare environment lowers the risk of a revenue miss. If this were fully priced, LUV would trade with peers rather than 26% below its 52-week high, with the skew still leaning to upside.
findings.independence: The United release is a separate document pointing the same way (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/100517/000010051726000184/ual_erx09302026xex991.htm).

findings.finding: The sector's reaction function this week is to look through fuel to revenue. UAL rose 5.2% intraday on 2026-10-21 (97.77 to 102.90 at 12:22 ET) after a Q4 EPS guide of $0.50-1.50 on $4.80 fuel, which its own update said is above consensus fuel. DAL was flat on its 2026-10-09 print (82.14 to 82.17). LUV is up 1.9% today in sympathy.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Southwest's own record runs against this: it has sold off on 5 of its last 7 prints, including both 2026 prints that carried guide cuts (-4.07% and -6.19%).
findings.why_not_priced: The UAL move is today's tape, and LUV has absorbed part of it (+1.9%). What is not yet in the price is whether the same looking-through extends to a lower-margin, unhedged, leisure-heavy carrier with no refinery and no premium cabin mix. The slightly upside-paid skew (-2.6) suggests the options market leans that way.
findings.independence: DAL's flat print-day reaction is a separate series (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/DAL?range=1mo&interval=1d).

findings.finding: TSA checkpoint throughput is down about 2% yoy. 9/21-10/20/2026 averaged about 2.51M a day against 2.55M for the day-of-week-aligned 9/22-10/21/2025 (-1.8%); September 2026 averaged 2.354M against 2.403M (-2.0%). That is consistent with fuel-driven fares rationing leisure volume, which is Southwest's core customer, against peers' premium-led growth.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None measured. Southwest has not reacted to an industry-volume series before in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: The series is public daily, and it is an industry proxy, not Southwest's own number. Southwest guided capacity -1% to flat, so lower volume mostly shows up as load factor, which peers report as roughly flat to down 1 point. Small by construction.
findings.independence: The 2025 comparison comes from https://www.tsa.gov/travel/passenger-volumes/2025. This is a proxy: United's domestic load factor of 84.4%, down 0.9pt, points the same way at company level (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/100517/000010051726000184/ual_erx09302026xex991.htm).

findings.finding: On 2026-08-10 Southwest replaced its 2016 revolver, which ran to 2028, with a $2B five-year revolver due 2031 (accordion to $3B), undrawn at signing. June 30 liquidity was $5.3B including the old $1.5B line, and gross leverage was 2.1x.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed reaction. It was filed in August with no price event.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced: public since August. I asked what the money buys and the answer is nothing specific. It is an undrawn, larger and longer backstop, routine rather than distress, so the sign is zero. It is filed because a fuel-squeezed Q4 makes liquidity a call topic.

findings.finding: Capital return has run dry. Southwest bought no stock in Q2 2026 after $1.25B in H1, and only $450M remains of the $2.0B authorization. Diluted shares were 493M in Q2 2026 against 541M a year earlier. With a large Q4 fuel headwind, a new authorization or faster pace is unlikely to be announced.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This was disclosed with the July print, which fell 6.19%; buyback news is not separable from that move.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: it lands inside what the company said in July. It is filed because a surprise in either direction, such as a new authorization or explicit suspension language, would land on the call.

findings.finding: Holder concentration at 9/30/2026: PRIMECAP 10.02% (49.0M shares, 13G/A amendment 21) and Franklin Templeton 10.2% (49.7M, including Putnam 7.6%). Two long-only holders own about 20% of the shares, which damps forced selling but does not set a direction.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and carries no direction. It is filed for the panel's positioning context only.
findings.independence: The Franklin 13G/A is a separate filing (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/38777/000003877726000259/primary_doc.xml).

baseline_tension: The net is a hair negative against a slightly upside-paid skew (-2.6) and a sector that was bought today. Southwest's own history (5 of 7 prints down, both 2026 guide cuts sold) supports the negative side, so the two roughly cancel and p_up sits near 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (bar unsourced; consensus not reachable this run): fuel-guidance finding capped from -1.2 to -1.0.
Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction; the market already marks fuel): Q3 fuel finding cut from -0.8 to -0.6.
Lesson 5 (a proxy is smaller than company-level peer numbers): TSA finding cut from -0.3 to -0.2.
Lesson 7 (the negative lean runs against a mild upside skew and a sector bid): p_up moved from 45 to 47, so expected_move_pct went from -0.70 to -0.42.
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): the revolver was checked (undrawn backstop, nothing specific funded) and left at 0.
Peer-print-after-the-company-spoke (the 'what has worked' section): kept both peer findings, revenue +1.0 and fuel -1.0, at full capped size rather than netting them.
